At one charge/discharge opportunity per rotation these imply about 2,573 and 4,234 cycles respectively. Schmitz Table 3 gives an 80% design input without cycle life. JPL reports Opportunity around 44–50% depth and over 5,000 cycles across its battery wet life. The Perseverance requirements specify over 2,010 cycles in three years at a maximum 60% depth. With the pinned kernel and unchanged night and efficiency, an illustrative 50% rather than 80% assumption increases incremental storage from 43.57 to 69.71 kg/kW. These comparators do not prescribe a design or predict current mission results. Distinct from rc-100 capacity and efficiency provenance and rc-627 worksheet citation wiring.

target_file: modules/calc.py; MODEL.md; campaign/verification_sheet.py; linked Spacecost operational_costs.csv
target_row: Mining reliability growth law and its handbook citation
field: Cumulative failure rate versus mission/wave probability
current_value: The pinned Economicspace calculator sets the failure probability of each mission in a wave to max((1-p_first) * (previous flights+1)^(-alpha), 1-p_mature). MODEL.md identifies the probability law as Duane/AMSAA and cites the handbook rate range. Spacecost describes the handbook rate as a failure probability over cumulative production.
proposed: Identify the current power law as a mission-level scenario inspired by reliability growth. Cite the handbook measure and document how missions or waves map to tested configurations. If adopting the discrete AMSAA model, use and calibrate its configuration failure probabilities with suitable data and show their effect on programme success. Carry the distinction into the worksheet and the Spacecost input note.
evidence: MIL-HDBK-189C §5.2.6.1 defines the original law on cumulative average failures per test time. §6.2.4.6 derives the discrete probability for an individual configuration from the increment of cumulative expected failures divided by its trial count. Using identical 0.85 first-wave success, alpha 0.30 and 0.95 cap for an illustration, the pinned and discrete-law means are 0.902431 and 0.924822 for ten serial missions and 0.905588 and 0.892117 for three waves of ten. One first wave alone gives 0.85 in both. This comparison is neither a fitted growth curve nor a validated mining reliability forecast. Distinct from rc-084 on the historical exponent range and rc-910 on replaying the calculator.

target_row: Synodic period and first departure wait
field: Ten-year scheduling cap versus computed physical synodic period
current_value: The model caps the returned synodic period at 10 yr, so its mean initial wait is at most 5 yr. The worksheet labels the capped value as the synodic period and MODEL.md illustrates the uncapped physical relation.
proposed: Expose the uncapped period and the separate scheduling assumption in the code, worksheet and documentation. Treat the cap as an explicit sensitivity unless an earlier feasible option is found under the stated delta-v, time and geometry constraints.
evidence: The archived 1.05 AU illustration gives approximately 14.2 yr uncapped. The installed 2000 SG344 orbit gives 28.776 yr via the same two-body relation. Both return 10 yr and a 5 yr modeled mean wait. Of 43,043 installed near-Earth rows in the function's valid semimajor-axis domain, 2,753 (6.40%) exceed 10 yr before capping. NHATS models trajectory windows jointly with delta-v and durations, and the OSIRIS-REx departure result is mission-specific. No feasible calendar is inferred from the raw period. Distinct from rc-235, which corrected the raw illustration.

target_row: Repeated campaigns with launch windows enabled
field: Calendar cadence, departure phase and rig campaign count
current_value: The model computes stay as digging plus half a synodic period and uses max(stay, synodic period) for the interval between successive waves, with no departure phase or window width.
proposed: Label the current cadence as a statistical approximation. For a programme intended to dispatch only in feasible windows, anchor later dispatches to the previous date and a mission window set, or specify a scenario that allows inventory staging or departures outside the preferred windows. Propagate the chosen calendar to rig life, finance and market windows.
evidence: Holding the first dispatch at 4.4 yr in a 3 yr dig and 2.8 yr recurrence fixture, the code gives 4.4 yr cadence and fits three campaigns in the 15 yr life. With one narrow usable epoch per period and no campaign overlap, a rig misses the immediately following epoch and dispatches after 5.6 yr, fitting only two campaigns. The third dispatch would move from 13.2 to 15.6 yr. The archived 2018 DT timing control keeps three campaigns in either case but changes cadence from 4.938 to 3.875 yr. NASA/JPL's InSight record illustrates finite periods; Bennu shows a target-specific return month. This is a fixed-window contrast, and rc-889 addresses the separate disabled-switch replay.

field: CH/CK composition description, CK density comparator and basis of phase assumptions
